015607: // --- Complex values -------------------------------------------------------
015608: //
015609: // A complex value is an ordinary two-field aggregate by the time it reaches
015610: // the IR (see c_ir_complex_type). Arithmetic uses scalar float opcodes and
015611: // constructs its result with the existing immutable AGGREGATE operation.
015612: // Known constructors expose their scalar operands directly; memory objects
015613: // and non-constructor values retain explicit field loads. Complex lvalues
015614: // keep their object identity. There is no separate complex opcode or cleanup
015615: // pass, and native backends keep the existing aggregate representation.
015616: //
015617: // Which arithmetic each operator gets is Clang's, checked against
015618: // `clang -O0 -S -emit-llvm` for every combination rather than derived:
015619: //   * `+` and `-` are componentwise, and a real operand touches only the real
015620: //     half (the imaginary half of the promoted real operand is a positive
015621: //     zero, and Clang carries the other operand's imaginary part through
015622: //     unchanged rather than adding it).
015623: //   * `*` and `/` with a real operand scale or divide both halves.
015624: //   * `*` and `/` with two complex operands call the compiler runtime --
015625: //     __mulsc3/__muldc3/__multc3 and __divsc3/__divdc3/__divtc3 -- which is
015626: //     what Clang emits without -ffast-math or -fcx-limited-range. Those
015627: //     helpers implement the overflow- and NaN-recovering forms from C11
015628: //     Annex G, and calling them rather than inlining Smith's algorithm is the
015629: //     choice made here: it is bit-for-bit what a Clang-built object does, and
015630: //     the alternative would be a second, subtly different implementation of
015631: //     the same numerics living in this file.
015632: //   * `real / complex` also goes to the runtime, with the numerator's
015633: //     imaginary part passed as a positive zero, again matching Clang.
015634: //   * `==` and `!=` compare both halves.
015635: //
015636: // System V x86-64 returns a `long double _Complex` in ST(0)/ST(1) (the psABI's
015637: // COMPLEX_X87 class) where the equivalent struct is returned in memory. That
015638: // is the one place the aggregate model is not the ABI, and it is the only
015639: // thing the backends had to learn about complex: the classifier gives that
015640: // result four X87/X87_UP eightbyte parts, the canonical x86-64 emitter pushes
015641: // the imaginary half and then the real one before its RET and pops them in
015642: // that order after a call, and every other position -- the argument, the
015643: // loads, the stores, the copies -- is the two-field aggregate unchanged.
015644: 
015645: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_float16_negate(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value, IrTypeId type_id, IrSourceRange source)
015646: {
015647:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015648:     IrTypeId bits_type = c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, C_TYPE_UNSIGNED_SHORT);
015649:     IrValueId slot = c_ir_emit_temporary(builder, type_id, source);
015650:     if (c_ir_type_is_ieee_binary16(builder, type_id) && bits_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
015651:         slot.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, slot, type_id, value, source))
015652:     {
015653:         IrTypeId bits_pointer_type = c_ir_add_pointer_type(builder->program, builder->pointer_types, bits_type);
015654:         IrValueId address = c_ir_emit_address_of_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
015655:         IrValueId bits_address = address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && bits_pointer_type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015656:                                      ? c_ir_emit_cast(builder, address, bits_pointer_type, source)
015657:                                      : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015658:         IrValueId bits_place = bits_address.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_dereference_place(builder, bits_address, source)
015659:                                                                               : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015660:         IrValueId bits = bits_place.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID ? c_ir_emit_load_place_raw(builder, bits_place, bits_type, source)
015661:                                                                       : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015662:         IrValueId sign_mask = c_ir_emit_integer_value_typed(builder, UINT64_C(0x8000), false, (CToken){0}, bits_type);
015663:         IrValueId flipped = bits.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && sign_mask.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID
015664:                                 ? c_ir_emit_binary_value(builder, bits, sign_mask, bits_type, IR_BINARY_INTEGER_BITWISE_XOR, source)
015665:                                 : IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015666:         if (flipped.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && c_ir_emit_store_place(builder, bits_place, bits_type, flipped, source))
015667:         {
015668:             result = c_ir_emit_load_place(builder, slot, type_id, source);
015669:         }
015670:     }
015671:     return result;
015672: }

015674: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_unary_value(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId operand, IrTypeId type, IrUnaryOperation operation,
015675:                                                     IrSourceRange source)
015676: {
015677:     IrValueId result = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015678:     if (operand.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID &&
015679:         operation == IR_UNARY_FLOAT_NEGATE && c_ir_type_is_ieee_binary16(builder, type))
015680:     {
015681:         result = c_ir_emit_float16_negate(builder, operand, type, source);
015682:     }
015683:     else if (operand.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID && type.value != IR_ID_UNDERLYING_INVALID)
015684:     {
015685:         result = c_ir_add_result(builder, type);
015686:         IrInstruction instruction = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_UNARY, type);
015687:         instruction.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
015688:         instruction.operands[0] = operand;
015689:         instruction.operand_count = 1;
015690:         instruction.unary_operation = (u8)operation;
015691:         instruction.result = result;
015692:         IrInstructionId id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, instruction, source);
015693:         builder->function->values[result.value].definition = id;
015694:     }
015695:     return result;
015696: }

015698: // GNU's `__real__`/`__imag__` and their unsuffixed spellings, as the unary
015699: // operator each names. The expression walker asks this of every identifier it
015700: // meets where an operand is expected, so the length test carries the common
015701: // answer before any comparison runs.
015702: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL bool c_ir_complex_part_operator(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, CToken token, CConditionalOperator* operation)
015703: {
015704:     if (token.kind != C_TOKEN_IDENTIFIER)
015705:     {
015706:         return false;
015707:     }
015708:     String8 spelling = c_token_spelling(builder->preprocess.spelling_base, token);
015709:     if (spelling.length != 6 && spelling.length != 8)
015710:     {
015711:         return false;
015712:     }
015713:     if (string_equal(spelling, S8("__real__")) || string_equal(spelling, S8("__real")))
015714:     {
015715:         *operation = C_CONDITIONAL_REAL_PART;
015716:         return true;
015717:     }
015718:     if (string_equal(spelling, S8("__imag__")) || string_equal(spelling, S8("__imag")))
015719:     {
015720:         *operation = C_CONDITIONAL_IMAGINARY_PART;
015721:         return true;
015722:     }
015723:     return false;
015724: }

015726: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrType* c_ir_complex_type_of(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId type_id)
015727: {
015728:     IrType* type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, type_id);
015729:     return type && type->is_complex ? type : 0;
015730: }

015732: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrType* c_ir_value_complex_type(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId value)
015733: {
015734:     if (value.value >= builder->function->value_count)
015735:     {
015736:         return 0;
015737:     }
015738:     return c_ir_complex_type_of(builder, builder->function->values[value.value].canonical_type);
015739: }

015741: // The complex type whose halves are `element`, or invalid when `element` is
015742: // not one of the three real floating types a complex type can be built over.
015743: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrTypeId c_ir_complex_type_for_element(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrTypeId element)
015744: {
015745:     CTypeKind kind = element.value == builder->f32_type.value            ? C_TYPE_FLOAT_COMPLEX
015746:                      : element.value == builder->f64_type.value          ? C_TYPE_DOUBLE_COMPLEX
015747:                      : element.value == builder->long_double_type.value  ? C_TYPE_LONG_DOUBLE_COMPLEX
015748:                                                                          : C_TYPE_INVALID;
015749:     return kind == C_TYPE_INVALID ? IR_TYPE_ID_INVALID : c_ir_builder_scalar_type(builder, kind);
015750: }

015752: // A field whose index is already known. Complex halves and anonymous aggregate
015753: // members have no C name to turn into a source token or look up again.
015754: BUSTER_C_INTERNAL IrValueId c_ir_emit_field_index_place(CIntegerIrBuilder* builder, IrValueId place, u32 field_index, IrSourceRange source)
015755: {
015756:     IrValueId next = IR_VALUE_ID_INVALID;
015757:     if (place.value < builder->function->value_count)
015758:     {
015759:         IrTypeId owner_type = builder->function->values[place.value].canonical_type;
015760:         IrType* owner = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, owner_type);
015761:         if (owner && field_index < owner->field_count)
015762:         {
015763:             IrTypeId field_type = owner->fields[field_index].type;
015764:             IrType* field_value_type = ir_type_from_id(&builder->program->types, field_type);
015765:             next = ir_function_add_value(
015766:                 builder->arena, builder->function,
015767:                 (IrValue){
015768:                     .canonical_type = field_type,
015769:                     .definition = IR_INSTRUCTION_ID_INVALID,
015770:                     .category = IR_VALUE_PLACE,
015771:                     .is_read_only = builder->function->values[place.value].is_read_only,
015772:                     .is_volatile = builder->function->values[place.value].is_volatile || (field_value_type && field_value_type->is_volatile),
015773:                 });
015774:             IrInstruction field = c_ir_instruction_initialize(IR_OPCODE_FIELD, field_type);
015775:             field.operands = arena_allocate(builder->arena, IrValueId, 1);
015776:             field.operands[0] = place;
015777:             field.operand_count = 1;
015778:             field.immediates = arena_allocate(builder->arena, u64, 1);
015779:             field.immediates[0] = field_index;
015780:             field.immediate_count = 1;
015781:             field.result = next;
015782:             IrInstructionId field_id = c_ir_append_instruction(builder, field, source);
015783:             builder->function->values[next.value].definition = field_id;
015784:         }
015785:     }
015786:     return next;
015787: }
015788: 
015789: // An addressable place holding `value`. An aggregate lvalue is already one, a
015790: // value that a load produced can reuse the place that load read (the same
015791: // recovery c_ir_emit_field_place_from_value performs for `x.member`), and
015792: // anything else -- a call result, a freshly composed value -- is spilled.
